facts.text: In late July the glacier up to the col can be hard ice in the early morning, so crampons matter; the steep patchy snow between the col and the south face may need a couple of crampon changes.
In early August the glacier showed a few patches of bare ice but mostly firm snow that cramponed easily, and the descent in afternoon warmth was straightforward with no need to re-fit crampons.
Above the lake the going is slow, loose talus and moraine, noticeably harder than the mileage suggests (August).
In early July a ditch cut across the road about a mile short of the trail start can stop low-clearance cars; budget extra walking if you cannot cross it.

notes: The Southwest track is a clean round trip from the border obelisk, where 4x4 parties drive to; our Trailhead pin is at the Chilliwack Lake Road spur much further out. I could not find a fetched official source giving a coordinate for the washout/road end, so no trailhead pin is proposed. The applier may need to accept a start at Monument 65.
